## Context

- Handlers can receive `json`, `body` (bytes), and query; there is no first-class support for **`multipart/form-data`** (file uploads) or **`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`** request bodies. Many HTML forms and legacy clients require this.
- See [Feature gaps](https://github.com/QueryaHub/OxyRoute/blob/main/docs/feature.md#2-запрос-и-тело).

## Direction

- Parse `Content-Type` in the dispatch path (or Python boundary): size limits, temp files / spool for large uploads.
- Expose e.g. `form` and/or `files` kwargs to handlers, or a typed `UploadFile`-like object—align naming with what Granian/RSGI allows for streaming.
- Reject or truncate oversized bodies with **413** when limits are configured.

## Acceptance criteria

- At least one pytest uploading a small file and reading form fields.
- Document limits and security notes in `docs/handlers.md`.

## Research

- Starlette `Request.form()`; RSGI body read is already a single `protocol()` read today—check whether multiple reads or streaming are needed for large files.
